description: Learning to act from reward: agents and environments, multi-armed bandits, Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, Monte Carlo and temporal-difference methods, Q-learning, policy gradients and deep reinforcement learning. Every algorithm is derived, implemented and watched learning in simulated grid worlds and control environments in the browser, taught to the depth of a strong final-year reinforcement learning course.
modelledOn: Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
Bertsekas, Reinforcement Learning and Optimal Control
outcomes: Formulate sequential decision problems as bandits or Markov decision processes with suitable states, actions and rewards.
Derive the Bellman equations and solve known MDPs with policy evaluation, policy iteration and value iteration.
Implement Monte Carlo, temporal-difference and Q-learning methods and analyse their bias, variance and convergence.
Apply function approximation and policy gradient methods, including actor-critic algorithms, to large and continuous problems.
Train and debug deep reinforcement learning agents and evaluate them with reproducible experiments.
Assess the risks of reward misspecification and unsafe exploration when applying reinforcement learning to real systems.

units.title: Agents, environments and rewards
topics: The reinforcement learning problem: agent, environment, state, action, reward, return; how it differs from supervised learning
Episodic and continuing tasks; discounting; the reward hypothesis and reward design
Environments as code: the Gymnasium interface, grid worlds, cart-pole, mountain car
Examples: game playing, robotics, recommender systems, irrigation scheduling and traffic signal control

units.title: Multi-armed bandits
topics: The exploration-exploitation dilemma; action-value estimates and incremental updates
Epsilon-greedy, optimistic initial values, upper confidence bound and Thompson sampling
Regret and its bounds; non-stationary bandits and constant step sizes
Contextual bandits: choosing which SMS reminder or promotion to send a mobile money customer

units.title: Markov decision processes
topics: The Markov property; transition dynamics and reward functions; finite MDPs
Policies, state-value and action-value functions
The Bellman expectation and optimality equations derived; optimal policies
Partially observable problems and belief states in brief

units.title: Dynamic programming
topics: Iterative policy evaluation; the contraction mapping argument for convergence
The policy improvement theorem; policy iteration
Value iteration; asynchronous and generalised policy iteration
The curse of dimensionality and why model-free methods are needed; an inventory MDP for a community pharmacy

units.title: Monte Carlo and temporal-difference learning
topics: Monte Carlo prediction: first-visit and every-visit; Monte Carlo control with exploring starts
On-policy and off-policy learning; ordinary and weighted importance sampling
TD(0) prediction and bootstrapping; the bias-variance trade-off between Monte Carlo and TD
n-step methods, eligibility traces and TD(lambda)
SARSA and expected SARSA for on-policy control; the cliff-walking comparison

units.title: Q-learning and function approximation
topics: Q-learning as off-policy TD control; convergence conditions; maximisation bias and double Q-learning
Model-based planning: Dyna-Q, prioritised sweeping, Monte Carlo tree search in brief
Value function approximation: linear features, tile coding, semi-gradient methods
The deadly triad of function approximation, bootstrapping and off-policy learning; divergence examples
Least-squares TD and fitted Q iteration

units.title: Policy gradient methods
topics: Parameterised policies: softmax and Gaussian; the policy gradient theorem derived
REINFORCE; baselines and variance reduction
Actor-critic methods; advantage estimation and generalised advantage estimation
Trust regions and proximal policy optimisation; natural gradients in brief
Continuous control: deterministic policy gradients, DDPG, TD3 and soft actor-critic

units.title: Deep reinforcement learning
topics: Deep Q-networks: experience replay, target networks, learning from pixels
DQN improvements: double DQN, duelling networks, prioritised replay, distributional methods
Engineering deep RL: hyperparameters, seeds, reward scaling, debugging learning curves, reproducibility
Exploration in hard problems: intrinsic motivation, curiosity and count-based bonuses
Offline reinforcement learning from logged data; reinforcement learning from human feedback for language models

units.title: Reinforcement learning in the real world
topics: Multi-agent reinforcement learning and self-play in brief
Reward misspecification, reward hacking and safe exploration
Simulation-to-reality transfer; recognising when reinforcement learning is the wrong tool
Capstone: an agent for a simulated problem such as microgrid battery scheduling or traffic lights at an Accra junction, with an experiment report

schedule.title: The reinforcement learning problem and environments
schedule.exercise: Define the agent, environment, state, action and reward for three problems (irrigation, traffic lights, recommendations), and write one reward function for each with a way it could go wrong.

tasks.title: Run a random agent in a grid world environment for 100 episodes and record the mean return and the episode length
Compute the discounted return of a given reward sequence for three discount factors and show how discounting changes the preferred action
Define an irrigation scheduling environment with state, actions and a reward in the Gymnasium interface, and test it with random and rule-based agents

schedule.title: Multi-armed bandits
schedule.exercise: Derive the incremental mean update and explain why a constant step size suits non-stationary bandits, then choose an exploration method for a promotions problem.

tasks.title: Run a 10-armed bandit with epsilon-greedy and watch the action-value estimates and average reward converge
Compare epsilon-greedy, optimistic initial values, UCB and Thompson sampling on a 10-armed testbed over 1000 steps
Build a contextual bandit that picks which SMS reminder to send mobile money customers, and compare its reward with a random policy

schedule.title: Markov decision processes and Bellman equations
schedule.exercise: Write the MDP of a small recycling-collection robot, derive the Bellman optimality equations for it, and solve for the values by hand.

tasks.title: Run through a four-state MDP in the visualiser and list the transition probabilities and rewards for each action
Solve the Bellman expectation equations for a three-state MDP and a fixed policy as a linear system, and state each value
Find the optimal value function and policy of a five-state MDP from the Bellman optimality equations, and verify it is a fixed point

schedule.title: Dynamic programming for MDPs
schedule.exercise: Explain why policy evaluation converges, using the contraction argument, and compare policy iteration with value iteration on a pharmacy inventory problem.

tasks.title: Run iterative policy evaluation on a 4 by 4 grid world and record the value table after each sweep
Run policy iteration and value iteration on the same grid world and compare the number of sweeps to the optimal policy
Model the stock of a community pharmacy as an MDP with demand uncertainty, solve it by value iteration, and compare the policy with a fixed reorder rule

schedule.title: Monte Carlo and temporal-difference prediction
schedule.exercise: Compute first-visit Monte Carlo and TD(0) estimates by hand for three episodes, and explain the bias-variance difference.

tasks.title: Estimate state values with first-visit Monte Carlo on a small random walk and track the error as episodes increase
Compare TD(0) and Monte Carlo prediction on a random walk over many episodes for several step sizes
Compare ordinary and weighted importance sampling for off-policy Monte Carlo evaluation and report the bias and variance of each

schedule.title: n-step methods and SARSA
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on how eligibility traces unify TD and Monte Carlo, and how SARSA and Q-learning differ on the cliff-walking task.

tasks.title: Run SARSA on cliff walking and trace the path that the learned policy takes
Compare 1-step, 4-step and TD(lambda) prediction on a random walk and choose the best setting
Run SARSA and expected SARSA on cliff walking, and explain the difference in the paths and online return

schedule.title: Q-learning, planning and function approximation
schedule.exercise: Show on paper how maximisation bias arises, and why double Q-learning removes it, using a two-state example.

tasks.title: Run Q-learning on a grid world and watch the Q-table converge to the optimal policy
Add model-based planning steps to Q-learning (Dyna-Q) and measure how many episodes are saved on a maze
Solve mountain car with tile coding and semi-gradient SARSA, tune the step size, and plot the learned value function

schedule.title: The deadly triad and batch methods
schedule.exercise: Write an explanation of why bootstrapping, off-policy learning and function approximation together can diverge, using Baird's counter-example.

tasks.title: Run the standard divergence example and watch the weights grow while the true values stay finite
Solve a prediction problem with least-squares TD and compare it with semi-gradient TD in data efficiency
Implement fitted Q iteration with a regression model on a logged data set, and compare its policy value with plain Q-learning

schedule.title: Policy gradient and actor-critic
schedule.exercise: Derive the policy gradient theorem step by step, and explain why a baseline lowers variance without adding bias.

tasks.title: Run REINFORCE on a small grid world and plot the return per episode
Add a baseline to REINFORCE and compare the variance of the return and the learning speed across ten seeds
Implement an actor-critic with generalised advantage estimation, tune lambda, and compare it with REINFORCE on cart-pole

schedule.title: Trust regions and continuous control
schedule.exercise: Explain in a note the clipped objective of proximal policy optimisation and why it limits policy change, and list when to prefer SAC over PPO.

tasks.title: Run PPO on cart-pole and plot the clipped objective's ratio and the learning curve
Change the clipping range in PPO across three values and report the effect on stability and the final return
Train a continuous-control agent on a pendulum task with SAC or TD3, and compare learning curves over three seeds

schedule.title: Deep Q-networks and engineering practice
schedule.exercise: Write a debugging checklist for a deep RL agent that does not learn, with five checks on rewards, scale, seeds and replay.

tasks.title: Train a small DQN on cart-pole with experience replay and a target network and plot return against episodes
Add double DQN and prioritised replay to a baseline DQN and compare their learning curves over five seeds
Debug a deliberately broken DQN that fails to learn, find the three faults in the reward scale, replay buffer and target update, and fix them

schedule.title: Exploration, offline learning and human feedback
schedule.exercise: Short essay: when is offline reinforcement learning better than online learning, and what are the risks of learning from human feedback?

tasks.title: Add a count-based exploration bonus to Q-learning on a sparse-reward maze and compare the episodes needed to find the goal
Train a policy from a fixed logged data set without interacting with the environment and compare it with the behaviour policy that logged the data
Solve a hard-exploration maze with intrinsic curiosity rewards, and report the exploration coverage against epsilon-greedy

schedule.title: Safety, transfer and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: describe the problem, reward design, algorithm choice, hyperparameters, seeds, learning curves and the failure modes of an agent for a simulated microgrid or junction.

tasks.title: Review five reward functions in a scenario, identify the loophole an agent could exploit in each, and propose a fix
Decide in a branching case whether a power utility should use reinforcement learning, a rule-based controller or optimisation, with evidence for each
Train an agent for traffic lights at an Accra junction or a microgrid battery, compare it with a fixed rule baseline over ten seeds, and report
